text: CHIEF DECISION LANDED as ADR 0002 D14a at f478525. storymodel4s.view compiles surface primitives into NarrativeScene.marks; SurfaceDetail is NOT a renderer-layer projection a consumer applies to SurfaceAtlas itself. DECIDING ARGUMENT, verified in source rather than reasoned: EvidenceHorizon is documented as 'the one evidence-horizon computation shared by every view compiler' (ADR 0002 D4 row 7) and it lives in view; V-L1, V-L2 and selectionPlacements are all properties of NarrativeScene.marks. MARKS A RENDERER ADDS ON ITS OWN ARE COVERED BY NONE OF THEM, so a consumer-side projection could render a token belonging to a narrative node the horizon HIDES - the precise leak class already fixed once tonight when the Atlas ancestor climb could reveal a placement reachable only through horizon-hidden evidence. DOES NOT WEAKEN D4's no-inference law: SurfaceUnit(id, kind, span, ordinal, parent) is canonical, already has stable ids and a parent chain, so compiling it is SELECTION AND PLACEMENT of existing units, not derivation of new claims. ACCEPTANCE BAR RECORDED IN THE ADR: until surface marks are compiled, SurfaceDetail must not be exposed as a control - exposing a selector over an inert axis would mint three identities for one representation and look like the feature had shipped.
